arguments.prompt:
Create exactly SIX new body-action drawings of the SAME Mourning Dove in the attached reference, on one transparent RGBA sprite atlas. The attachment is a3-column by2-row conditioning atlas: each768-square cell is an EXACT COPY of the same old standing source. These repeated originals are framing/identity guides only, not the desired output poses. Return a3:2 atlas, exactly3columns by2rows of equal SQUARE cells, ideally1536 by1024 overall with512-square cells. No gutters, labels, gridlines or extra birds. One bird in each cell.

CRITICAL SCALE AND FRAMING: preserve the whole reference-cell composition, same bird individual and anatomy size in every cell. Do not zoom in, recenter, crop to the body, fit each pose's bounding box, or enlarge birds to fill cells. The standing source is a768-square canvas with large empty margins. At192-square full-cell output its visible length is118pixels and its image support root is105,150, with pink toe references97,149 and116,149. Scale the entire reference CELL uniformly to the returned native CELL, including those margins; do not compare a returned cell to the whole3x2 reference atlas. Each new action has the SAME head/torso/limb anatomical scale, with honest changing pose envelopes. Keep the grounded feet/support region near the same cell locations for bath phases. Root/cell coordinates are metadata, not visible markers.

Preserve the detailed naturalistic pixel-art Mourning Dove identity: small pale gray/tan rounded head, dark round eye with fine blue eye-ring, small narrow charcoal bill, subtle dark cheek spot, warm buff/pink-tan breast, brown-gray foldedwing feathers with diagnostic dark oval spots, long slender pointed tail with pale edges, pink legs and toes. Same palette, fine intentional feather clusters, restrained antialiasing and light direction. Not a pigeon with a broad bill, not a duck, no collar, crest or cartoon eye. Avoid random pale pixel speckle, glossy outline or airbrushed style.

Read cells left-to-right, top row then bottom row. Draw six unmistakably DIFFERENT real body/wing/neck/leg keys, not a static bird shifted up/down:
1 APPROACH: calm slight forward lean and one cautious short-step foot posture approaching shallow water; still the same relaxed dove, folded wings. This is an approach-ready key, not a whole walking loop.
2 SETTLE: both feet supported, legs bend and breast lowers into a shallow bath posture; neck relaxes and feathers loosen a little, wings slightly loosened from the body. Not an airborne hop.
3 DIP: feet remain supported; body tilts and head/neck bend forward/down, narrow bill dipping toward an imaginary water surface near output y144, roughly6pixels above the ground boundaryy150. Actually redraw curved neck and head, not just translate the standing bird. No invented long legs.
4 WING FLUTTER: low supported bathing stance, wings genuinely lift/open partly away from body with fanned feather structure, one distinct vigorous but grounded bathing wing shape. Keep body anatomical scale; wings may extend naturally into unused margins. Not flight/takeoff, no duplicate wings or motionblur.
5 SHAKE: another genuinely different supported pose, head/neck turned and body feathers visibly fluffed in a compact wet-feather shake key, wings returning closer to sides. Show changed feather silhouette and body anatomy rather than a blurred/translated copy.
6 EXIT/PREEN: body rises back up, one cautious exit-step posture with the head turned backward and bill touching shoulder/wing feathers in a clear grooming key. Preserve species proportions and supported-leg logic; no floating body.

This is an authored shallow-water-bathing proposal, not measured footage. Do NOT draw the water, bath vessel, floor, branch, splashes, droplets, shadow, backdrop, text or contact markers: bird-only isolated RGBA in all six cells, with fully transparent surroundings. Keep every wingtip/tail/toe inside its OWN cell and retain generous framing. Six actual new action keys only; the exact old awake will be reused separately, so do not waste a cell on another identical neutral or blink.
